subject: Staggered onramp schedule & discount triggers for Neptune Systems (AWS marketplace)
messages:
From: Ethan Walters <ewalters@neptunesys.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neptune Systems Procurement <procure@neptunesys.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Evaluations + marketplace purchasing cadence — looking to align MAP to AWS purchase

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick note from procurement and our platform team: we're preparing an evaluation sprint on our ingestion and retrieval workload and we'd like to map that to a Marketplace purchase path so we can move to purchase through an AWS private offer at the end of the eval.

Key asks from our side:
- Can Redwood provide a staged onramp schedule that ties evaluation milestones to specific private-offer pricing steps?
- We prefer a 30–45 day technical eval (pilot) with a capped-credit allowance before committing. If the pilot meets success criteria, procurement wants a 3-month initial commit with escalator discounts at defined usage thresholds.
- Any constraints on how private offers need to be structured in AWS Marketplace? Procurement needs the timeline by Aug 8 to include in our quarter planning.

I've attached a short scope doc with the baseline tests we're running (eval-scope.pdf). Happy to jump on a call this week.

Regards,
Ethan
Head of Platform Engineering
Neptune Systems
[Attachment: eval-scope.pdf (PDF)]

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Walters <ewalters@neptunesys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluations + marketplace purchasing cadence — looking to align MAP to AWS purchase

Ethan — thanks for the clear scope. Good news: we can align a staged onramp to an AWS marketplace private offer, and we will propose discrete discount triggers tied to MAP milestones so procurement sees predictable economics at each step. Below is a concise proposal to get us moving; Ben and Rachel are looped for ops/legal/marketplace confirmation.

Proposed staged onramp (high level):
1) Pilot (30 days): 0–50k tokens/day equivalent — Redwood provides $8k in credits; success gates: 3 end-to-end test runs passing, <150ms p50 response for retrieval route, qualitative sign-off from Eng. No billing in Marketplace yet.
2) Proof-of-value (next 60 days): 3-month paid commit via AWS private offer. Minimum commit: $45k over 3 months. Pricing step 1 applies (base rate).
3) Ramp & discounts (post-commit): automatic per-month tiered discounts when monthly usage crosses thresholds: 100k/month -> 7% discount; 300k/month -> 12% discount; 600k/month -> 20% discount. Discounts applied at private-offer billing reconciliation.
4) Contingency & fallback: if KPIs not met at end of pilot, option to extend pilot for 30 days with adjusted credit.

Operational notes:
- We'll draft the MAP (attached MAP-draft.docx) with exact acceptance criteria and measurement windows.
- Pricing table attached (pricing-v1.xlsx) shows list and discounted steps; final private-offer will reference the agreed tiered schedule.
- Rachel, can you confirm whether the AWS private-offer flow requires minimum committed monthly billing to unlock tiered discounts? Ben, please flag any marketplace constraints.

Next steps:
- I can host a 30-minute alignment with procurement this week to walk through the MAP and the private-offer mechanics. If that works, propose Wed 11:00 PT.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachments: pricing-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet), MAP-draft.docx (docx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Evaluations + marketplace purchasing cadence — looking to align MAP to AWS purchase

Folks — quick ops note from the marketplace side: AWS private offers can support tiered pricing but there are operational trade-offs we should bake into the MAP. A few suggestions: 

1) Make the discount triggers calendar-based windows (e.g., measured monthly with a 7-day reconciliation window) — this avoids disputes over usage spikes.
2) For the 3-month initial commit, set an explicit minimum monthly invoice amount (e.g., $15k/month) so Marketplace will accept the private-offer structure and downstream billing.
3) Add a "burst capacity" clause for QPS spikes during ramp so Neptune can temporarily exceed tiers without immediate penalty (bill at next tier rate but credit applied in the following month if sustained).
4) Legal redline note: avoid retroactive discounts; all discounts must be forward-applied after the reconciliation period.

I'm fine with the high-level numbers Vanessa proposed but would like Rachel to confirm acceptance criteria wording and any procurement-specific verbiage we need for the PO flow.

Ben
Senior Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
[Internal attachment referenced: marketplace-constraints.txt]

From: Neptune Systems Procurement <procure@neptunesys.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Ethan Walters <ewalters@neptunesys.com>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Evaluations + marketplace purchasing cadence — looking to align MAP to AWS purchase

Vanessa / team — thank you, this aligns with procurement's needs. We reviewed the MAP draft and the staged onramp looks acceptable pending the marketplace constraints you noted. Procurement requests:

- Finalize MAP with exact pass/fail metrics and the calendar-based reconciliation windows as Ben recommended.
- Send the DocuSign envelope for the 3-month initial commitment SOW and provide the AWS private-offer link once DocuSign is executed so we can cut the PO in time for our Aug 8 planning deadline.

We'll sign off on the pilot credits and move to the private-offer commit after acceptance. Please send the DocuSign and the private-offer URL; we will route the PO internally once signatures are complete.

Thanks — looking forward to the Wed alignment call if you want to keep it.

Procurement Team
Neptune Systems
[Attachment: PO-template.pdf (PDF)]
